name: Potato of Life — Spatial Map
purpose: A spatial and relational model of the Potato of Life. It maps the potato as a measurable object first, then maps project-defined vertical, horizontal, interior/exterior and threshold relationships.
epistemic_rule: Spatial measurements and biological observations are empirical when sourced. The vertical architecture, symbolic directions and Jesus Door are project-defined interpretive models unless independently evidenced.
core_idea: Treat the Potato as a spatial object with boundary, interior, exterior, surface, points, axes, orientations, layers, openings, sections, hidden regions, exposed regions, trajectories and transformations.

measurement_schema.rule: Measurements must retain units, method and uncertainty. Estimates must be labelled estimates.

spatial_layers.meaning: rooting, absorption, connection and buried life
stored energy, body, memory and potential
localized transition from stored potential to outward growth
skin and interface between interior and environment
section through which the hidden interior becomes visible
visible life, light capture, exchange and expansion
reproduction, return and continuation of the cycle

potato_of_life_spatial_model.construction: two equal circles whose centres are separated by one radius; their intersection forms the lens-shaped vesica-piscis
mathematical_properties: lens width along centre line = radius
intersection points form equilateral-triangle geometry with the two circle centres
perpendicular bisector is a symmetry axis

project_mapping.vertical_axis: Axis connecting upper and lower fields
project_mapping.intersection_points: upper and lower limits of the central interface
project_mapping.circles: distinct domains that become relational through overlap

potato_of_life_spatial_model.important_constraint: The mathematical construction is real geometry; the Father/Son/Heaven/Jesus Door assignments are the project's symbolic interpretation of that geometry.

door_in_the_wedge.physical_analogy: A cut wedge creates a new exposed face through which the previously hidden interior can be seen.
door_in_the_wedge.project_reading: The wedge is a model for Door because it converts an enclosed object into an object with an accessible interface without destroying the identity of the whole.
questions: What becomes visible after the cut?
Does the opening have a centre, width, orientation or direction?
What is preserved and what is transformed?
Can this model be represented mathematically?

topological_questions: What remains invariant if the potato is deformed without cutting it?
What changes when it is cut?
When does a boundary become a passage?
Can an eye be treated as a point, region or interface?
Is the Door better represented as a point, line, region, surface or volume?
What is the topology of whole, wedge, cavity and exposed interior?

research_program.phase_1_measure: Collect real 2D/3D potato measurements, including dimensions, volume, surface shape, eye number, eye spacing, eye depth and curvature.
research_program.phase_2_model: Build point-cloud or mesh representations and identify axes, surfaces, boundaries, sections and growth points.
research_program.phase_3_geometry: Construct the Potato of Life vesica-piscis independently of the physical potato and record exactly which dimensions are project-defined.
research_program.phase_4_overlay: Test overlays between physical potato geometry and symbolic geometry without forcing alignment.
research_program.phase_5_transform: Apply rotation, reflection, scaling, cutting and projection to determine which relations persist.
research_program.phase_6_cross_scale: Test whether the same spatial grammar appears from cell to tuber to plant to farm to food system to world system.
research_program.phase_7_comparison: Apply the same measurement and relation vocabulary to other objects and systems as controls.
research_program.phase_8_synthesis: Separate genuine invariants from visual coincidences, metaphors and intentional symbolic constructions.

things_to_map_that_are_easy_to_miss: time as a spatial-like dimension of growth
completion_test: A physical potato can be represented as a measured spatial object.
Its boundary, interior, surface, eyes, axes and sections can be queried.
The Potato of Life geometry has exact mathematical definitions.
The wedge/door analogy has an explicit spatial model.
The mandorla is represented as an intersection region rather than merely a word.
The Jesus Door is linked to the mandorla as project-defined symbolism.
Spatial relationships resolve to canonical IDs.
Failed spatial correspondences remain recorded rather than discarded.
